title: Passes for Miami Beach in 1942 and 1957
summary: He and the interviewer compare the pass system for black people on Miami Beach; he needed a police card in 1957 and could not play there in 1942.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I remember going down to Florida in the early '50s for vacation, it was the first time I was in Florida, and I remember the black people had to be off Miami Beach by a certain time. If they had to be there, they needed some kind of a pass.
Well, you need a pass to go on at that time, you know --
Well, yeah, but I know even before, when I was there in 1942, you needed a pass just to go on the beach. You couldn't go on Miami Beach.
Unless you were working there, you know.
(Inaudible) hotels had to be out of there by a certain time and if not, they had to have a pass.

See, I was working -- I was there in -- when was it I went down there, in '57 I went down there, it was. You had to have a pass then. You had to have a police card. Yeah. But it was a lot different than it was -- in fact,
in '42 you couldn't play out there. But people survived those things, and I think the strongest people survived.
